messages:
Nina (People Ops): Heads-up: quick clarification thread on late review submissions, remediation steps, and reviewer crediting for this cycle. TL;DR: we allow limited late handbacks + a remediation process for impacted employees; managers must follow the steps below.

Rahul (Eng Manager): What counts as a late submission vs missed?

Nina (People Ops): Missed = handback not completed by window close and no approved extension. Late = submitted within 72h after close with an automatic 'late' flag. Missed after 72h becomes manual exceptions (requires people-ops).

Priya (Reviewer): If a review is late, does that change calibration handling?

Nina (People Ops): Good Q. Late submissions still go into calibration but are flagged. We run a separate "late bucket" calibration slot so anchors from late reviews don't bias the main meeting. Managers should add a 1-line context note when submitting late (cause + reconciliation plan).

Ava (IC): I had reviewer assigned but they turned red (overloaded) and review got delayed. What happens to my comp cycle?

Nina (People Ops): If delay pushes your packet past comp freeze, we create a remediation packet for the next compensation run. People-ops + your manager will add an addendum explaining timing. This should be rare; escalate asap.

Rahul (Eng Manager): Process steps for managers when a direct report's handback is late or missed?

Nina (People Ops): Follow this 4-step remediation: 
1) Submit the Late/Missed form: https://rwd.in/late-review with root cause and proposed reviewer.
2) If reviewer was overloaded, mark reviewer capacity in the roster and request floating reviewer.
3) Add a one-line "late context" to the submission (e.g., reviewer overloaded, LOA, tooling import error).
4) Confirm with people-ops to see if compensation freeze is impacted. People-ops will respond within 24h.

Ops-Bot: Reminder: Late/Missed form auto-creates a ticket and pings people-ops on weekdays.

Priya (Reviewer): How do we credit reviewers who pick up overtime reviews? We had a bunch last cycle and it felt invisible.

Nina (People Ops): We track reviewer credit in two places: reviewer-activity roster (visible in the console) and quarterly reviewer appreciation (spot bonuses / kudos). If you pick up an overtime review, note it on the form and cc people-ops. We'll credit the reviewer for workload balancing.

Ava (IC): What about changing PIP or performance status during late remediation? Manager question — can we move someone onto/out of a PIP mid-cycle?

Nina (People Ops): No unilateral changes to PIP status during an open handback or remediation window. PIP actions require a separate HR case and must be recorded before handback opens. If you think a PIP is warranted, open an HR case (hr-cases@redwood.com) and keep the review thread focused on evidence only.

Rahul (Eng Manager): Any export/import tips? We had one CSV import fail and that caused a 24h hold last time.

Nina (People Ops): Use the template exactly: columns order fixed, filenames match the pattern in the playbook. If import fails, include the import log in the Late/Missed form so we can triage faster.

Priya (Reviewer): For accountability, can people-ops share weekly late-report summaries with managers?

Nina (People Ops): Yes. We'll publish a weekly "handback health" summary (counts by team, late vs missed, average resolution time) every Friday. Expect it to start next week.

Rahul (Eng Manager): Thanks. One last: do late flags affect eligibility for promotions this cycle?

Nina (People Ops): No — late flags alone don't disqualify promotion eligibility. Promotions are evaluated on the evidence in the packet and calibration outcomes. However, persistent process noncompliance (repeated late handbacks across a manager or reviewer) will trigger an operational review.

Ava (IC): Appreciate the clarity. I'll flag my lead about the reviewer credit rules.

Nina (People Ops): Great 44d If anyone needs an immediate exception (LOA, emergency), DM me and file the formal LOA so we can grant the 72h extension or manual exception.
